findings.title: Pre-announcement: Plone security fix 20261110
findings.summary_md: The Plone/Zope Security Team gave eight days of warning that a remote code execution fix would ship on Tuesday 10 November 2026 around 1300 UTC, affecting all Plone 6 branches (6.0, 6.1, 6.2) and older releases back to at least Plone 4.3. Because details would become public at release, the team urged operators to pre-emptively block URLs containing portal_modifier and published working rewrite and location rules for Apache, nginx and Traefik, plus a caveat that Varnish does not decode percent-encoding before matching. The post notes that an AI tool might be able to build an exploit from the pre-announcement alone, so the workaround should not wait for patch day.

findings.title: Add server rule to mitigate Plone security issue 20261110 (isaw.web issue 621)
findings.summary_md: A public Plone operator opened an urgent-labelled issue five days before patch day to add a reverse proxy rule blocking any path containing portal_modifier, since the coming fix would only cover supported Plone 6 releases. The issue was assigned the same day and closed as completed on 6 November 2026 with the workaround applied, showing that the portal_modifier block was already being deployed in the wild before the advisory details existed.

findings.title: Products.CMFEditions advisory GHSA-67qm-q795-jh7h: missing security declarations on modifier classes
findings.summary_md: The lead advisory for the chain rates the flaw CVSS 3.1 9.8 with vector AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H, CWE-862. ConditionalModifier and ConditionalTalesModifier in Modifiers.py, plus the size-guard modifiers AbortVersioningOfLargeFilesAndImages and SkipVersioningOfLargeFilesAndImages in StandardModifiers.py, declare no security, so methods with docstrings including edit are publishable without a permission check and an anonymous visitor can change a modifier's TALES condition and then run it. The fix protects edit with Manage portal and the accessors with View management screens, and makes the size-guard hooks private. Credit goes to Mokrane Abdelmalek reporting through the Ghent University VDP.

findings.title: Plone security hotfix 20261110
findings.summary_md: The vendor advisory describes a five-flaw chain that lets an anonymous visitor run code on the server: Products.CMFEditions modifier classes with no security declarations, overly broad allow_module declarations in Products.CMFPlone, Products.MimetypesRegistry and plone.batching that expose imported names such as os to restricted code, and plone.restapi exposing the standard library json module so json.dump and json.load can call protected methods without the required permission. Fixes ship as Products.CMFPlone 6.2.3, 6.1.6 and 6.0.16 with matched CMFEditions, MimetypesRegistry, plone.batching and plone.restapi versions, or as Products.PloneHotfix20261110 for any release from 4.3 to 6.2 on Python 2.7 and 3, with a Zope restart required. CVE numbers were requested but unassigned at publication, and the post warns that details being public makes exploitation by AI-assisted actors likely.

findings.title: Products.CMFPlone advisory GHSA-92qw-564p-pmg6: overly broad allow_module declarations
findings.summary_md: This critical advisory covers the allow_module declarations in Products.CMFPlone that opened whole modules, and everything those modules import, to restricted code. TALES expressions and Python Scripts could therefore escape the restricted Python sandbox and reach modules including os, which is the component of the chain that converts a logic flaw into code execution.

findings.title: oss-sec: Plone security fix 20261110: remote code execution
findings.summary_md: The full advisory was mirrored to oss-sec roughly ten hours after the vendor posted it, carrying the same five security advisories with GitHub advisory links, the fixed package versions for 6.0, 6.1 and 6.2, and the Products.PloneHotfix20261110 fallback for releases back to 4.3. The mailing list copy is what put the package-level detail in front of the general security audience rather than only Plone operators.

findings.title: Plone Unauthenticated RCE, Fixed in 6.2.3 (Hotfix 20261110)
findings.summary_md: Ostorlab's write-up frames the chain as five flaws (four Critical, one Medium for plone.restapi), rates the lead issue CVSS v3.1 9.8 and CWE-862, and records that no CVE was assigned, no exploitation was known and the flaws were absent from the CISA KEV catalog as of 11 November 2026. It stresses the acquisition angle: portal_modifier is reachable at any depth, and because one flaw also fires when an editor saves versioned content, an internet-unreachable instance still has an internal path to code execution with the Zope process's privileges.
